# Stand Firm When the Ground Shakes
## Scripture
"Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that in the Lord your labor is not in vain." – 1 Corinthians 15:58
## Reflection
The world around us is always shifting—cultures change, opinions flip, and the ground beneath our feet can feel unsteady. But Paul calls men to something different: to be steadfast and immovable. That's not stubbornness; it's rootedness. A man who is immovable isn't one who never feels the tremors—he's one whose foundation is deeper than the shaking.

Notice the connection Paul makes. Being steadfast isn't passive. It's paired with "always abounding in the work of the Lord." Stability fuels action. When you know your labor in Christ is never wasted, you can keep showing up—at your job, in your marriage, in your church, in your quiet battles no one sees. The world may call your faithfulness pointless. God calls it treasure stored up.

Ask yourself today: where have I been drifting? Where have I let fear or fatigue make me pull back? Anchor yourself again in the risen Christ. He is the immovable rock, and because He lives, your labor is not in vain.
## Daily Challenge
Do 3 sets of 20 squats, holding each rep at the bottom for two seconds—and while you hold, thank God that He is your firm foundation.
